task_description: Give the Continuum .ipa the UI it has never had, starting with the half that makes it playable. The app works and is unplayable: on master (merge 922fc5f) all five cores run real commercial games at 60 fps with 0 dropped frames on an iPhone 17 Pro Max, but there is no input wiring whatsoever. apply_gamepad is never called from Swift, there is no touchesBegan, no DragGesture and no control buttons, there is no way to leave a running game and no visible pause. The user has been watching intro screens unable to press Start. The agreed design reference is the old browser prototype's UI, recorded in .kiro/steering/product-scope.md with screenshots in docs/. This task PLANS the whole UI effort and IMPLEMENTS STAGE 1 ONLY. Stage 1 (FEAT-001, FEAT-002) is a real player screen with working touch controls: a back control that stops the session and returns to the library, the emulated picture aspect-correct on black, a thin telemetry strip, and per-system touch controls wired to the engine and pushed every frame so held buttons stay held, with the D-pad tracked as ONE surface so diagonals resolve and full multi-touch so a direction can be held while a face button is pressed. Stage 2 (FEAT-003, FEAT-004, FEAT-005) is the Netflix-style library, real cover art and Settings: PLANNED IN DETAIL, NOT BUILT. Stage 3 (FEAT-006) is the user-editable control layout the user asked for plus the engine FFI additions the remaining player controls need: PLANNED, NOT BUILT. FEAT-007 records the Android .apk the user wants after the iOS work is finished: RECORDED ONLY, and it shaped no Stage 1 decision. ABSOLUTE CONSTRAINTS: Swift only, under native/ios/, with every new file registered in native/ios/project.yml under targets.Continuum.sources because that list is explicit and an unlisted file is silently not compiled. Do not touch crates/** (Rust), scripts/**, .github/**, native/ios/build-engine.sh or native/ios/package-ipa.sh. Keep every architectural invariant: the import-and-copy flow and its picker delegate lifetime machinery, filenames preserved on import, no security-scoped URLs on the launch path, engine.coreState as the only source of truth for residency, ensureCoreLoaded after stopSession, CoreCatalog's single routing table, LibraryEntry identity on absolute path, one MTLDevice owned by Rust, exactly one engine.launch call site. Keep every diagnostic string reachable. No em dashes. A distinct status string on every failure path. Commit locally on branch ios-ui-player-controls; do not push, do not open a PR, do not trigger CI.

verification.semantic_review: not run as a separate pass; the by-eye review this stack requires was done against the five things swiftc -frontend -parse provably cannot check, and each is recorded in FEAT-001 and FEAT-002 findings: the apply_gamepad array order and length, UITouch identity across began/moved/ended, the D-pad surface maths, safe-area and orientation layout, and @MainActor isolation around EngineHost.
verification.summary: Stage 1 implemented; Stage 2 and Stage 3 planned only, as scoped. swiftc -frontend -parse on all four Swift files under native/ios/ (ContinuumApp.swift, MetalCanvas.swift, TouchControls.swift, PlayerScreen.swift): exit 0 each. This is a SPELL-CHECK ONLY, so the input contract, multi-touch tracking, layout and actor isolation were reviewed by eye and are documented per feature. python3 yaml.safe_load on native/ios/project.yml: valid, and both new Swift files are listed under targets.Continuum.sources. cargo test: 74 passing, proving no Rust changed. git diff --name-only: only native/ios/** plus .agents/tasks/task-ios-ui-player-controls/**. No em dashes in any changed file. THE CENTRAL FINDING, which the task was explicitly warned not to guess: apply_gamepad takes the W3C standard gamepad order, NOT libretro's joypad index order, traced uniffi_api.rs:548 -> bridge.rs:554 -> input/gamepad.rs apply_standard_gamepad and its STANDARD_GAMEPAD_MAP. Per-system mappings were read from the upstream core sources rather than assumed, which corrected the Mega Drive pad: A B C are retro Y, B, A. The .ipa build and every on-device behaviour are verified ONLY by the orchestrator's CI run and a device test afterwards.
